eli5.text: A specific user identified by the ID ending in 17c42b037329 is now prevented from using the chat service and will receive a message saying the system is overloaded if they attempt to. This affects anyone who tries to interact with the assistant using that account. If you checked the chat system today, you'd see that user can no longer get responses and instead gets an error message indicating the service is temporarily unavailable.

ai.title: Add GPT-5.2 and propose tools to editor agents
ai.summary: GPT-5.2 replaces GPT-5.1 in `editor-implementor` and `best-of-n` selectors. New `propose_str_replace` and `propose_write_file` tools allow agents to draft changes without immediate application, enabling review workflows. `editor-multi-prompt2` becomes the default max-tier editor, spawning both Opus and GPT-5.2 implementors. Context pruning logic updated to remove redundant subagent spawn messages.

eli5.text: Starting today, the coding assistant that works behind the scenes in Claude's integrated development environment has been upgraded to use a newer, more capable model (GPT-5.2) for generating code, and it now has a new workflow where it can draft suggested changes and send them to a second AI to review before applying them. If you ask Claude to make a significant code change, you will now get suggestions produced by the upgraded model and evaluated by both the existing assistant and the new one before anything is written, giving you a better chance of a correct and clean edit.

ai.title: Extract v1 route helpers for web-search and docs-search
ai.summary: New `web/src/app/api/v1/_helpers.ts` centralizes JSON parsing, API key auth, and credit charging logic previously duplicated in `docs-search/_post.ts` and `web-search/_post.ts`. `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts` refactors `callWebSearchAPI` into a generic `callCodebuffV1` handler with typed field extractors. `linkup-api.ts` exports `LinkupEnv` and extracts header serialization to `headersToRecord`.

eli5.text: The code that powers web search and document search now shares one common set of tools for parsing requests, checking API keys, and charging credits, instead of each route keeping its own copies. As a result, search requests are handled through a single internal pathway that can extract fields from incoming data more consistently, and header information from search responses is read in a uniform way. If you use these search features today, nothing about how you interact with them changes, the work is behind the scenes, tightening up how the system checks your access and bills you without altering the search behavior itself.

ai.title: CLI auth revalidation and env var migration
ai.summary: Auth revalidation triggers on token change via SHA-256 hashed query keys in `use-auth-query.ts`. `API_KEY_ENV_VAR` deprecation forces migration to `getCiEnv().CODEBUFF_API_KEY` across `auth.ts`, `index.tsx`, and hooks. Logger context updates consolidate into helper functions in `use-auth-state.ts`.

eli5.text: You will now be prompted to re-authenticate automatically when your login token changes, instead of the system silently reusing an old session. Behind the scenes, the app stopped depending on a legacy name for the secret API key and now reads the key from a single, consistent source whether you are running locally or in a continuous-integration pipeline. If you use the CLI in a CI environment, set the key under the new name; the old name it looked for before is no longer read.

ai.title: Enforce package boundaries with typed env accessors and test defaults
ai.summary: CLI and core packages replace direct `process.env` reads with typed `getCliEnv()` and `getSystemProcessEnv()` accessors, enforcing package boundaries and preventing cross-package env pollution. `common/src/env.ts` now injects `TEST_ENV_DEFAULTS` during test runtimes and uses `safeParse` for validation, while `bunfig.toml` adds a preload hook to ensure these defaults apply before SDK execution. Scope covers `cli/src/utils/env.ts`, `common/src/env.ts`, and test fixtures like `agent-runtime.ts`. New env vars `ZED_TERM`, `ZED_SHELL`, and `CODEBUFF_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER` are added to the `CliEnv` type, and `parseGitignore` now silently skips unreadable ignore files.

eli5.text: If you run the Codebuff command-line tool, your terminal settings (including new scroll speed and Zed editor detection) now load through a single, locked-down source instead of being read loosely from anywhere in the system. The tool also sets up default settings automatically whenever you run automated checks, so tests behave the same way every time without needing manual setup. What you'd notice: your scroll speed and terminal theme detection stay consistent across different shells and test runs, and the tool no longer accidentally mixes your personal environment variables with its own.

ai.title: Analytics env config now injected instead of lazy-loaded
ai.summary: common/src/analytics.ts now accepts explicit clientEnv config via initAnalytics and configureAnalytics, replacing lazy require of @codebuff/common/env. web/src/lib/server-init.ts passes env to initAnalytics. Analytics config is stored in module-level analyticsConfig and PostHog client is initialized only when envName is prod.

eli5.text: The analytics setup now gets its configuration information passed to it directly at startup, rather than fetching it behind the scenes whenever it's needed. This means when the website starts up on the server, it explicitly provides the environment settings (like which version it's running - production, development, etc.) to the analytics system, instead of that system trying to look it up on its own later. The analytics client (PostHog) only gets fully initialized when it detects it's running in the production environment, skipping setup entirely in development and testing scenarios. This is a behind-the-scenes change that makes the system more predictable and easier to manage, but doesn't change any visible features or behavior for users.

ai.title: Reduce editor token waste
ai.summary: Prompt tweaks in editor-implementor2.ts ban final summaries to save tokens, as only file changes are passed on. editor-multi-prompt2.ts reorders strategies array to put default first. Internal prompt and logic adjustments in .agents/editor/best-of-n/ files.

eli5.text: The AI coding helper has been told to stop writing final summary messages after it finishes making code changes, since only the actual file edits matter and long explanations just waste time and computing resources. It also now tries the default version of its approach first before attempting alternatives, which slightly changes the order in which it generates different versions of a solution. These are behind-the-scenes adjustments to how the internal coding agent works, so you wouldn't notice any difference in the code itself, but it helps the system run more efficiently.

ai.title: base2-max-evals agent disables askuser and suggestfollowups
ai.summary: New agent definition `base2-max-evals` extends `createBase2` with `noAskUser: true`, stripping `ask_user` and `suggest_followups` from its toolset. `createBase2` in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` gains the `noAskUser` option, conditionally filtering these tools and omitting the corresponding system prompt guidance. This ensures the evals orchestrator runs autonomously without interactive prompts. Internal change to `.agents/base2` definitions only.

eli5.text: A new automated helper called the 'Buffy the Max Evals Orchestrator' has been added to run evaluation tasks without interrupting anyone for input. It skips the usual prompts that ask you questions or suggest next steps, so it can operate entirely on its own. If you were watching an evaluation run, you'd notice it no longer pauses for confirmation or recommendations. This change is part of the internal agent definitions and is already in place.

ai.summary: gpt-5.1 replaces gpt-5.2 as the default model for lite mode in the code editor. The `createCodeEditor` factory now maps `gpt-5` to `openai/gpt-5.1` instead of `openai/gpt-5.2`. Change scoped to `.agents/editor/editor.ts`.

eli5.text: The lighter version of the code-editing tool now uses an earlier version of its language model. If you use the tool in lite mode, you will get responses from the model that was previously used before a newer one was tried. The change only affects which model runs under the hood when the editor is asked for its default helper.

ai.title: Move xml-parser to common, drop backend and npm-app from CI matrix
ai.summary: parseToolCallXml moved to common/src/util/xml-parser.ts. packages/internal re-exports from @codebuff/common. web trace-processing imports direct from common. backend and npm-app removed from .github/workflows/ci.yml matrix.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to understand tool instructions written in simple tags like <type>click</type>, there is now just one place in the codebase that does that translation, used by both the command-line tool and the web dashboard. The old duplicate copy in the internal package now just points to that single shared spot, so anything running in a browser gets a version that stays browser-safe. Automated stability checks and test runs no longer waste time spinning up unused pieces of the system that haven't been touched. What you'd notice if you looked today is a cleaner flow with one less place for the XML-parsing logic to drift out of sync.

eli5.text: When you copy something in the chat, the little tooltip that explained the copy button now disappears right away instead of lingering. The copy button, which used to sit next to the timestamp on your messages, now appears inline with your message text, so it stays close to what you actually copied. If you watched this happen, you'd see the button pop up near your message content and the hover hint vanish instantly after clicking.

ai.title: pluralize includeCount option
ai.summary: Add `includeCount` option to `pluralize` in `common/src/util/string.ts`. Enables label-only output (e.g., 'question') by omitting the numeric prefix when `false`. `cli/src/components/blocks/ask-user-branch.tsx` uses this for skipped/answer headers.

eli5.text: When the tool asks you to pick between branches or review skipped questions, the labels it shows you now read more naturally, "Your answers:" instead of "Your 3 answers:", because the numeric count is no longer tacked onto words like 'question' and 'answer' in those headers. This makes the prompts feel less robotic and more conversational while you're interacting with them. The change is live today in the command-line interface.
